title: Expert Synthetic Aperture Radar
description: About this positionAs a SAR expert at TNO you truly work in the frontline of airborne – and spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar technology.If you are up to being challenged in an environment that is among the top in the world and if you are excited at the prospect of working with experienced colleagues on designing, and evaluating novel SAR systems and algorithms, and related airborne- and spaceborne radars, this might be your chance! We offer a stimulating environment with world-renowned experts and career opportunities that match what you do best - today and in the future.You will work at the Compact Radar Technology department within the Defence, Safety and Security unit of TNO. At this department we passionately work on technological breakthroughs for state-of-the-art RF sensor systems. Technology is changing extremely fast, resulting in new threats to the safety of our society but also in chances to realize what was not possible before.What will be your role?Traditionally large radar system have to be reduced in size for today’s platforms such as unmanned aircraft, small drones, and small satellites. TNO is developing new radar technology for such compact radar applications. As a SAR expert, you will perform both theoretical performance analyses as well as modelling and specification of new air- and spaceborne radar system concepts, with a good understanding of both the RF- and digital processing aspects of such systems. You will also be involved in test and evaluation of experimental systems up to TRL 7 level of maturity. Senior applicants may also become technical lead of system developments with a good understanding of technical requirements definition- and management, and of system engineering practices.As Europe’s leading R&D partner in the field of radar technology, TNO’s Radar Technology department develops anything from complete system concepts and architectures to integrated microwave circuits and antennas. We research and apply novel techniques like compressive sensing, deep learning and quantum radar technology. We have a large and strong team of radar engineers, software engineers, hardware developers, EM/antenna designers and other experts, who come together in an open-minded atmosphere to respond to the needs of our clients. We are driven by a desire to make technological breakthroughs and we welcome your ideas. What we expect from youYou are an analytical and structured team player that communicates easily with colleagues from different areas of expertise and different backgrounds. You are passionate about RF sensors, signal processing, system engineering, and aerospace applications, and you possess real-world experience with SAR image formation, SAR algorithms, and SAR system design. You can express yourself clearly when explaining the intricacies of air- and spaceborne radar to clients and other stakeholders. Other knowledge and skills you bring to TNO:A Master’s Degree or PhD in electrical engineering, or physics.A scientific background in one or more of these fields: radar imaging, radar design, signal processing, SAR algorithms, RF electronics and antennas.Working knowledge of MATLAB and/or Python.Working knowledge of System Engineering principles and practices.System Engineering experience is regarded as a particular plus for your application.What you'll get in returnChallenging and varied work with a real impact. And plenty of opportunities as, at TNO, you are in charge of shaping your career. We offer a gross monthly salary between € 4.819 and € 8.072 (based on your knowledge and experience), 8% holiday pay, a 13th month bonus of 8.33% and a flex budget (5.58% + € 180). In addition, you will be given every opportunity to develop yourself.TNO offers optional employee benefits, enabling you to tailor your benefits package to match your personal situation. You may also expect:An extremely professional, innovative working environment where colleagues are leading experts in their field.The opportunity to attend courses, workshops and conferences, and to receive training and coaching based on your needs.33 days annual leave plus a flexible holiday that can be used on a cultural, religious, or otherwise important day of your choosing (on a full-time basis).An employer working towards a respectful, inclusive, and equitable work environment where every employee can flourish, with various initiatives such as Jong TNO, numerous expertise based guilds, Rainbow Community and Round Tables on diverse inclusion topics.We offer a comprehensive and flexible mobility plan that also includes full compensation for public transportation for commuting and business travel.Great social events with your team and other TNO colleagues. title: Internship | Agent-based modelling of bird migration through wind farms
description: About this positionTwice a year, once in Spring and once in Summer, millions of songbirds traverse the Netherlands during their seasonal migration. As offshore wind energy is rapidly expanding, migratory birds may fly in proximity to wind turbines, thereby facing an increased risk of collision. If we can successfully simulate birds flying through offshore wind farms, we can improve predictions of collision risks during these mass migration events and/or improve wind farm layouts and operations to reduce those risks.What will be your role?At TNO, we are developing an agent-based model to simulate the flight of migratory birds through offshore wind farms. The model aims to capture a range of behaviours, from macro-avoidance of entire wind farms to micro-avoidance and collision risk at the level of individual turbines. In this project you will further adapt this agent-based model to (1) simulate bird flight behaviour as realistically as possible based on actual measurements, and (2) use the model to test how different wind farm layouts affect predicted collision risks. The insights of this model will support ecological impact assessments and can help in improving the design of future nature-inclusive wind farms.What we expect from youWe are looking for a student with an interest in both ecology and modelling, with strong quantitative skills. title: Internship | Cloud Resource Models for Virtual Core
description: About this positionThe growing deployment of latency-sensitive applications such as autonomous systems, industrial automation, augmented reality, and private 5G networks is driving a strong demand for edge computing infrastructures capable of hosting cloud-native network functions close to end users. In this context, resource models that estimate the performance of Cloud-native Network Functions (CNFs) deployed on Commercial-Of-The-Shelf (COTS) hardware under varying workloads, resource allocations, and deployment conditions are becoming increasingly important. These models enable operators to forecast key performance indicators such as throughput, latency, packet loss, and resource utilization before deployment or scaling actions occur.This internship focuses on the research and development of a model of compute infrastructure whose purpose is to facilitate CNF deployment optimization. You will work with our team on the analysis of CNF resource use and contribute to solutions that help advance the models used for network optimization. You will be part of an environment where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcome, and you have the space to develop your expertise.What will be your role?The performance of user plane CNFs deployed on COTS computing platforms is influenced by numerous interacting factors, including compute resources, virtualization layers, memory behavior, I/O subsystems, deployment configurations, and packet processing mechanisms. The relationship(s) between these factors and their impact on packet forwarding is very complex, making the development of reliable and scalable performance models challenging.During the internship, you will address this challenge with an empirical approach. You will develop and deploy a representative experimental environment in our lab which can generate reliable performance measurements. The experiment runs will target a device under test (DUT) which is a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) cloud compute host running containerized XDP-based User Plane Functions (UPFs). The emphasis with the runs is on understanding the bottlenecks and system features of both traffic generation and forwarding via the DUT. You will then analyze the experiment results and choose the most important factors and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), which will be included in the development of a resource model that predict the performance of CNFs deployed on the COTS machine.The overall goal is to combine system operation, development, benchmarking and modelling knowledge to enable more representative models of infrastructures running the cloud-native user-plane of next generation networks.What we expect from youWe are looking for a master student with a background in Computer Science and/or Engineering who has an interest in Computer Networking. You have basic skills in operating systems, coding in C/C++ and Python, or the motivation to quickly develop them. It helps if you have knowledge of Linux networking, eXpress Data Path, packet generation and queueing theory, but we are happy to support you in developing your knowledge in these areas. What matters most is that you are curious, proactive, and enjoy working together on the performance of networking workloads in virtual environments. This work can be scoped as an internship or as a MSc thesis project, depending on your need.What you'll get in returnAn internship at TNO means working in an environment where substance and impact are central. title: Internship | Design of phased array in E-Band for future SATCOM applications
description: About this positionFuture satellite communication systems need to transmit increasingly large amounts of data. Moving towards higher frequencies, such as E-band, can provide the required capacity, but it also creates new challenges for antenna design. The antennas must generate highly directional beams, scan over a wide angular range and operate efficiently despite the losses associated with these frequencies.This internship focuses on the development of a novel antenna array for future E-band satellite communication systems. You will work with our antenna research team to investigate different array technologies and identify promising solutions for efficient, wide-angle beam scanning. Your work will contribute to the development of advanced antenna systems that can support future high-capacity satellite links.You will be part of a collaborative research environment where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcomed and you will have the opportunity to further develop your expertise in antenna design and electromagnetic simulation.What will be your role?During this internship, you will investigate and compare different phased-array antenna technologies suitable for E-band satellite communications. You will assess their expected performance and explore the main trade-offs related to efficiency, scanning range, complexity and practical implementation.Based on this analysis, you will select one or more promising concepts and design antenna elements that can operate efficiently while supporting a wide beam-scanning range. You will use electromagnetic software simulators (e.g. Ansys HFSS or CST studio suite) to model, simulate and optimize the proposed designs.The internship will include different phases, such as:Reviewing relevant antenna-array technologies and design approaches;Defining performance requirements and comparison criteria;Modelling and comparing suitable array concepts;Designing and optimizing wide-scanning antenna elements in CST;Evaluating parameters such as efficiency, impedance matching, radiation pattern and scanning performance;Documenting the results and presenting recommendations for further development.The exact focus of the assignment can be refined together based on your interests, background and the results obtained during the first stages of the internship.By the end of the internship, you will have developed practical experience in antenna-array design, electromagnetic simulation, technical decision-making and the communication of research results. Your findings will support the selection and development of antenna technologies for future satellite communication systems. This internship is in the framework of a project between TNO and Viasat.What we expect from youFor this internship, we are looking for a university student pursuing a M.Sc. degree with a background in electrical engineering, telecommunications, applied physics or a related discipline. Knowledge of antennas, electromagnetics, microwave engineering or phased arrays will help you get started.Experience with Matlab and/or Python, Ansys HFSS and/or CST studio suite or the motivation to quickly develop them. It helps if you bring good communication skills, result driven attitude, and focused in problem solving, but we are happy to support you in developing areas you want to learn more about. What matters most is that you are motivated to develop these skills and are interested in applying theoretical knowledge to a practical antenna-design challenge.The intended duration of the internship is 9 months, with some flexibility depending on the requirements of your study program.What you'll get in returnAn internship at TNO means working in an environment where substance and impact are central. title: Internship | Modelling of photo-driven green syngas formation
description: About this positionConversion and storage of sustainable energy is one of the key challenges of the 21st century. At TNO, sustainable energy storage and conversion are addressed through the development of advanced materials and processes for green H2 production CO2 utilization. To enable a future energy system based on renewable electricity, innovative solutions are required that combine materials science, reaction engineering, transport phenomena, and reactor design. Therefore, TNO is looking for an enthusiastic MSc student who wants to contribute to the development of next-generation energy technologies.What will be your role?In this project, an experimental and modelling study will be performed on green CO formation from CO2 and H2 using light. Creating insights in how photons, reactants and heat interact is the core of this assignment. Furthermore, the research focuses on understanding how material properties, heat transfer, mass transfer and reaction kinetics affect the performance of green CO production. The work will include (Comsol Multiphysics) model improvement and validation with field data originating from the Interreg Foton project. For further details, visit project-foton.nl.The internship will last for at least 6 months, longer is possible if preferred by the candidate.What we expect from youYou are a proactive and independent MSc student in Chemical Engineering.Knowledge and affinity with advanced transport phenomena, including heat transfer, mass transfer, fluid dynamics and reactor engineering, is essential. Strong interest in physical chemistry and reaction kinetics is required.Experience with COMSOL Multiphysics is considered a major advantage. Good communication skills in English, particularly for presenting your work and writing reports, are expected.Depending on the requirements of the university, the project can be combined with an MSc thesis.What you'll get in returnAn internship at TNO means working in an environment where substance and impact are central.
